headline: Highest risk is medium: OpenMetadata’s MCP/API surfaces can create prompt-injection and data-leakage paths when paired with LightZero, but LightZero itself has no I/O or write capabilities.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes MCP, APIs, SDKs, events, and webhooks, so it can carry attacker-controlled content into downstream consumers. LightZero has no direct I/O surfaces, but if its outputs are manually or programmatically fed into OpenMetadata workflows, instruction-like content could be misread. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests LightZero-generated text into an MCP or webhook workflow without provenance filtering, injection is plausible.
IF an operator copies LightZero output into OpenMetadata fields that are later interpreted as instructions, the pathway exists.
mitigations: Disable any OpenMetadata workflow that auto-parses free text as instructions.
Add provenance tags to all LightZero-derived content before ingestion.
Review MCP tool schemas for prompt-like fields.
Use a manual approval step before acting on OpenMetadata-sourced text.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation between instructions and data.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, semantics, and memory/tribal knowledge, which can include sensitive metadata. LightZero has no filesystem read/write or network egress, so it is not itself a leak source, but OpenMetadata’s APIs/MCP/webhooks can move data outward. Because the pairwise data flow is inferred from docs-only profiles, the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF sensitive metadata is loaded into OpenMetadata and then exposed through APIs, SDKs, webhooks, or MCP, leakage can occur.
IF LightZero outputs are copied into OpenMetadata records containing sensitive fields, those fields may be redistributed.
mitigations: Restrict OpenMetadata API tokens to least privilege.
Turn off outbound webhooks unless required.
Mask sensitive metadata fields before cataloging.
Keep LightZero outputs out of shared metadata records.
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction and export controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and uses APIs/SDKs/events/webhooks, but no overlapping write surface with LightZero is documented. The only plausible conflict is indirect orchestration, which is weak and low blast radius.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable resource, contention could appear.
IF OpenMetadata writes to a shared backend that LightZero also mutates through an undocumented bridge, conflict is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid sharing mutable git or filesystem state.
Use per-agent credentials for OpenMetadata.
Serialize any shared-resource updates.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared backends.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata can consume and publish metadata through APIs, events, and webhooks, so it may treat upstream content as authoritative. LightZero produces game-playing outputs, but no verification layer between the two is documented. If LightZero-derived facts are imported into OpenMetadata and then propagated, errors can cascade across multiple work products.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are imported into OpenMetadata without validation, downstream metadata can inherit errors.
IF OpenMetadata triggers events or webhooks from unverified LightZero-derived records, the cascade expands.
mitigations: Require human review before publishing LightZero-derived metadata.
Validate imported fields against source-of-truth records.
Mark LightZero outputs as untrusted in OpenMetadata.
Disable auto-propagation from unverified records.
requires-engineering: add schema validation and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. OpenMetadata touches governance and memory/tribal knowledge, but LightZero has no declared sensitive-data handling. The compliance pathway is therefore weak and mostly depends on external deployment choices, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF a deployment stores regulated data in OpenMetadata without matching controls, compliance issues can arise.
IF LightZero is used in a regulated workflow that feeds OpenMetadata, policy gaps may surface.
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling before deployment.
Avoid placing regulated data in OpenMetadata by default.
Review retention settings in OpenMetadata.
Document the workflow’s residency assumptions.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
